children: Wacker Chemie said it had received roughly 171 million euros, equivalent to $195.8 million, for the partial sale of its stake in the German manufacturer of semiconductor wafers Siltronic.

The German chemical company said late Tuesday it had sold approximately 2.2 million shares for 77.25 euros each to institutional investors, a price constituting a discount to the stock's closing price on the same day of 82.75 euros.
The placement corresponds to 6.7% of Siltronic's stock and reduces Wacker's shareholding to approximately 15%.

Wacker said the sale strengthened its financial position, and gave it the ability to invest elsewhere. The company has been selling down its stake and netted around 188 million euros after selling 2.1 million shares in May.

The European chemical sector has been suffering under high energy costs, which have dented competitiveness. The continuing conflict between Iran and the U.S. has added to the challenges, having unleashed chaos across the oil and petrochemical sector. Oil and gas supplies have been curtailed, energy costs have risen and supply chains have been stretched.
In May, Wacker said it would lift prices in response to the higher input costs and also reached agreements to cut around 10% of its workforce.
Under new financial targets set out earlier this month, Wacker said cost savings and tightened investment criteria would lead to margin growth.
